title: lockrot explanation
description: The document `composer lockrot --explain=vendor/package --format=json` prints: the finding as the report carries it, and everything it was read from. Objects are open: a field added later validates against this file unchanged; the number in the id changes only when a field is removed or renamed.

version.description: The lockrot release that wrote the document.

schema.description: The document schema number this file describes.

php.description: The entry's php requirement, null when it has none.

released.description: The lock's `time` for the installed version, as Composer wrote it. A release's date only where the repository dated the version by one: for a branch snapshot it is the commit's (`branch_snapshot` is then true), and for a subtree split's tag it can be the date of a commit the tag shares with others. `metadata.installed_release` is the date lockrot reads as the release's.

repository.description: The entry's `source` URL, else its `support.source`, as a report may show it: a URL without its userinfo, query and fragment, a remote without a scheme without its user, and a path or a `file://` URL, which locate the machine that wrote the lock, by its last segment alone (`.../lib`; `...` for a home directory), which is where `finding.origin.local` is true. Null when the entry names none.

from_composer_repository.description: True when the lock entry carries a Composer `notification-url`. Composer writes one only for a package served by a `type: composer` repository that advertises a notify URL (`notify-batch` or `notify` in its packages.json); packagist.org and Private Packagist do. lockrot asks a repository for metadata, advisories and repository activity only about such an entry. False otherwise: a `path`, `vcs`, `artifact` or inline `package` repository entry, and also a package from a `type: composer` repository that advertises no notify URL (asset-packagist.org; a Satis build without `notify-batch`). lockrot asked no repository about a false entry, so the finding has no metadata, advisories, activity or libyears. True does not mean packagist.org. Stays a boolean for 1.x: the finer account of where an entry came from is `origin`, and this key is true exactly when `origin.kind` is `packagist` or `composer`. Same value as the finding's `from_composer_repository`.

metadata.description: What the Composer repository said about the package; null when it could not be loaded.

activity.description: What the repository host said; null when the repository was not checked.

project_php.description: The project's own `require.php` as composer.json writes it, the second floor each branch row's admits_project_php is tested against (its lowest version); null when composer.json names none or there is no composer.json. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

note_details.description: The run's notes, typed, exactly as the report's `note_details` carries them: one entry per `notes` string, at the same index. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it; from 0.13.0 on it is always written.

flaggedPriority.description: The priority order without `none`: the levels a step of a finding's `priority_basis` moves between. The same order as `priority`, restricted; not a set of its own.

priorityStep.description: One step of a finding's `priority_basis`: why it was taken, and the level before and after it. A step that could not move the level has `from` equal to `to`; up or down is the direction from `from` to `to` in the priority order.

reason.description: Why the step was taken: `transitive` (no direct requirement names the package, and one reaches it: `chain` has two or more entries), `unreached` (no direct requirement the run knows reaches it: `chain` is empty, as in a run without composer.json; the same step down as `transitive`, named apart so the page need not read `chain`), `dev` (the finding's `dev` is true) or `no_fix_expected` (the finding's `no_fix_expected` names an advisory). The first three lower the level one step, never below `low`; the last raises it one step, never above `critical`. An open set: a later release can add a step; read an unknown value as "other" and show it as written with its `from` and `to`.

noFixAdvisory.description: One advisory a finding's `no_fix_expected` names, and why no fix is expected for it.

id.description: The `id` of one of this finding's S9 advisories (`data.advisories[].id`), unique within the finding. Not promised to be a Packagist id: any Composer repository can serve advisories.

reason.description: Why no fix is expected, the first that applies: `not_on_installed_branch` (the finding is left-behind and the advisory's `fixed_by` names a release on a higher branch, which the installed branch will not get), `releases_unknown` (S9's `releases_read` is false: the release list was not read or the installed version could not be compared, so no fix was looked for, and this is not a prediction), `affected_range_unknown` (the advisory's `affected_versions` is null, so no release can be read as fixing it), `no_release_fixes` (the releases were read, the range is known, and no listed release above the installed version is outside it). An open set: a later release can add a reason; read an unknown value as "other" and show it as written.

signalId.description: A signal identifier: `S` and a number for lockrot's own, as `docs/verdicts.md` lists them, or `<vendor>:<name>` for one that does not come from lockrot. An open set: a later release under this schema number can add an id, so read one you do not know as "other". `x-known-values` lists the ids this release writes; read it as the enum to hold a document to them.

finding.description: The same object the report's `findings[]` carries; see report-1.json for the per-signal `data` shapes.

from_composer_repository.description: True when the lock entry carries a Composer `notification-url`. Composer writes one only for a package served by a `type: composer` repository that advertises a notify URL (`notify-batch` or `notify` in its packages.json); packagist.org and Private Packagist do. lockrot asks a repository for metadata, advisories and repository activity only about such an entry. False otherwise: a `path`, `vcs`, `artifact` or inline `package` repository entry, and also a package from a `type: composer` repository that advertises no notify URL (asset-packagist.org; a Satis build without `notify-batch`). lockrot asked no repository about a false entry, so the finding has no metadata, advisories, activity or libyears. True does not mean packagist.org. Stays a boolean for 1.x: the finer account of where an entry came from is `origin`, and this key is true exactly when `origin.kind` is `packagist` or `composer`. Same value as `lock.from_composer_repository` in this document. Absent from documents written before 0.13.0; from 0.13.0 on every finding carries it.

origin.description: See report-1.json. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

replacement.description: On an abandoned finding, the package its repository names as the replacement, when that is a Composer package name; null otherwise. Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

replacement_url.description: The page packagist.org keeps for `replacement`, an absolute https URL lockrot writes when packagist.org is the registry that named the replacement: the one whose metadata marked the package abandoned or, where lockrot read no metadata, the one the lock entry came from. Null when `replacement` is null, and for every other registry: Private Packagist keeps no public page, and WP Packages marks no package abandoned. lockrot does not ask whether the page exists. Show a link only when it is a string; read it, never build it from `replacement`. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

chain.description: From the direct requirement down to this package; empty when none reaches it. See report-1.json.

libyears.description: Years behind the newest stable release (a lower bound when that release is undated), at least 0. Null when not measured; from 0.13.0 on, `libyears_unmeasured` says why. Absent before 0.11.0. See report-1.json.

priority_basis.description: How `priority` was reached; see report-1.json. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

no_fix_expected.description: See report-1.json: absent before 0.13.0, null where the verdict makes no fix prediction, otherwise the advisories no fix is expected for.

last_stable_dated_by.description: The monorepo last_stable_release was read from through its `replace` list, null when it is the package's own.

installed_release.description: When the installed version released, as far as lockrot trusts a date for it: the lock's own `time`, or the monorepo parent's tag of the same version for a split package it dated (the split's own tag is dated by a commit other tags share, and the lock copies that date). The installed end of the finding's `libyears`. Null where neither is trusted: a branch snapshot, a lock entry without a `time`, or a split package whose installed version the parent does not date. Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

installed_release_dated_by.description: The monorepo parent whose tag `installed_release` is, null when it is the lock's own date or there is none. Optional, as `installed_release` is.

repository.description: The highest stable release's `source` URL, else its `support.source`, shown as `lock.repository` is. Null when it names none.

branches.description: Every release branch the repository lists, highest first.

highest.description: The branch's highest stable tag as the repository prints it.

highest_released.description: That tag's release date; null when the repository leaves it undated or dates it only by a commit other tags share.

highest_commit_date.description: The shared commit's date when highest_released is null for that reason.

newest_dated.description: The branch's newest dated stable release.

dated_by.description: The monorepo this row's dates were read from, null when they are the package's own.

php.description: The php requirement of the branch's newest dated release, as the repository lists it; of its highest tag when the branch has no dated release; and on a row the monorepo dated (`dated_by`), the package's own release's requirement, not the parent's. Null when it requires no PHP. The requirement S8 holds the branch against the project's own php and the target PHP. Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

admits_target_php.description: Whether `php` admits the target PHP: true when some version of the target minor (`target_php`, 8.4 read as >=8.4.0 <8.5.0) satisfies it, false when none does and Composer resolving against the target would not install the branch. Null is no answer, never admitted: `php` is null or cannot be read. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

admits_project_php.description: Whether `php` admits the lowest PHP the project's own `require.php` (`project_php`) promises: `>=7.2.5` and `^7.2.5 || ^8.0` both read as 7.2.5. Only the lowest is tested, as S8 tests it. Null is no answer, never admitted: `php` is null or cannot be read, or the project names no lowest PHP (no `require.php`, `*`, or one that cannot be read). Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

php_blocked_by.description: S8's admission test on this row's `php`: `project` when admits_project_php is false, else `target` when admits_target_php is false, else null. Null covers both admitted and untested (the admits_* fields tell them apart); S8 counts an untested branch as within reach, too. Every row carries it, whatever its place; S8 applies the test only to dated branches above the installed one, and the row of the newest branch it names carries its `floor_source`. On the installed row, `project` means the release `php` is read from, the installed branch's newest dated release (which may be the installed version itself or a newer one; see `php`), does not admit the lowest PHP the project's own `require.php` promises; misses_project_php says how it misses that floor. php_blocked_by does not by itself say the installed version does not admit it: that version's own requirement is `lock.php`. Values grow in minor releases; treat one you do not know as other. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

misses_target_php.description: Which side of the target PHP `php` is on when it admits no version of the target minor (admits_target_php false), read against the whole minor as admits_target_php reads it (8.4 as >=8.4.0 <8.5.0): `needs_newer` when every PHP `php` admits is above the floor (a newer PHP is needed), `stops_before` when every PHP it admits is below the floor (the branch's support ends before it), `skips` when it admits PHP both below and above the floor but not the floor itself (`^7.4 || ~8.2.0` against 8.1), `unsatisfiable` when it admits no PHP at all (`>=9 <8`, or only a branch name). Null exactly where admits_target_php is not false: the floor is admitted, or there is no answer. Given for the target whatever php_blocked_by names, so a row the project already holds back still says how it misses the target. On the installed row it describes the branch's newest dated release, which may be the installed version itself or a newer one (see `php`); that version's own requirement is `lock.php`. The page quotes `php` as written; no bound is extracted from it. Values grow in minor releases; treat one you do not know as other. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

misses_project_php.description: Which side of the project's floor `php` is on when it does not admit it (admits_project_php false). The floor is the lowest PHP the project's own `require.php` (`project_php`) promises, as admits_project_php reads it: `>=8.2` and `^8.2 || ^8.4` both read as 8.2, so `needs_newer` means newer than that lowest version, not newer than every version the project allows. `needs_newer` when every PHP `php` admits is above the floor (a newer PHP is needed), `stops_before` when every PHP it admits is below the floor (the branch's support ends before it), `skips` when it admits PHP both below and above the floor but not the floor itself (`^7.4 || ~8.2.0` against 8.1), `unsatisfiable` when it admits no PHP at all (`>=9 <8`, or only a branch name). Null exactly where admits_project_php is not false: the floor is admitted, or there is no answer. Given whatever php_blocked_by names. On the installed row it describes the branch's newest dated release, which may be the installed version itself or a newer one (see `php`); that version's own requirement is `lock.php`. The page quotes `php` as written; no bound is extracted from it. Values grow in minor releases; treat one you do not know as other. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

packageOrigin.description: Where a lock entry came from, as lockrot tells it from the entry and the manifest's own `repositories`, without asking any repository: `kind`, the `registry` where lockrot can name it, and the package's page there. Nothing in it is copied from the entry's URLs or the manifest's: a login, an organisation or a machine path is never written. Open: a later minor release may add a member.

package_url.description: The package's page on `registry`, an absolute https URL lockrot writes for a registry that keeps a public page per package name (`packagist.org`, `wp-packages.org`), from the name the lock records. Null for any other registry, for a name that is not a Composer package name, and for every kind but `packagist` and `composer`. It is the page the registry keeps for that name; whether this run's repositories still list the package is the finding's `note`. Show a link only when it is a string; read it, never build it, from `registry`, the name or anything else.

local.description: Whether Composer installed the package from the machine it ran on rather than from a server: a `path` or `artifact` repository, or a dist or source that is a path or a `file://` URL (a VCS repository checked out on the disk). Where it is true, `lock.repository` and `metadata.repository` in an explanation show the path by its last segment (`.../lib`). Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it; from 0.13.0 on every origin does.

originKind.description: What lockrot could tell about where the lock entry came from. `packagist`: its notification-url reports to packagist.org (packagist.org, or a mirror that keeps packagist.org's notify URL). `composer`: its notification-url reports to any other host (Private Packagist, WP Packages, Drupal, a Satis with a notify URL, a registry lockrot does not know, or a definition that declares one itself). These two are exactly the kinds whose `from_composer_repository` is true. `path`: its dist is a local directory (a `path` repository). `vcs`: its source is a VCS repository the manifest lists. `artifact`: its dist is an archive inside an `artifact` repository the manifest lists. `package`: an inline `package` definition in the manifest gives exactly this entry. `unknown`: none of these could be decided: a `type: composer` repository that advertises no notify URL (asset-packagist.org, a Satis without one, some packagist mirrors), a repository listed before the one that matches that could have served the name, a VCS repository renamed or removed since, or a run without composer.json. lockrot's kinds are lower-case words; `<vendor>:<name>` is reserved for a kind that does not come from lockrot. A kind keeps its meaning and its `from_composer_repository` value. An open set: a later minor release can add a kind, which may take entries out of `unknown`; read one you do not know by `from_composer_repository`, show it as written, and link nothing. The order of `x-known-values` is not the order lockrot decides in.

originRegistry.description: The Composer repository the entry came from, named by the host its notification-url reports to, when lockrot knows it: `packagist.org`, `repo.packagist.com` (Private Packagist; the organisation is never written), `wp-packages.org` or `packages.drupal.org`. `packagist.org` exactly when `kind` is `packagist`. Null for every other kind, and for a Composer repository lockrot does not know, whose host is not written: a private registry's host stays out of a published report. A label, never a template: build no URL from it. An open set: a later minor release can name another registry.

noteDetail.description: One thing the run could not see: `code` says what, `data` the facts, typed per code by the branches below, and `text` the sentence every format prints. A note whose code this schema does not list carries any object as its `data`: show its `text`, link its `docs_url` when it is not null, ignore its `data`, and still honour its `sets_network_failures`.

text.description: Exactly the `notes` string at the same index: prose, not contract. Key on `code` and `data`, never on the wording.

docs_url.description: An absolute https URL on lockrot.dev for this code; null means no page, show no link; read it, never build it. Every URL lockrot has written keeps resolving for all of 1.x, though the page it opens may change.

sets_network_failures.description: Whether this note is part of why the root `network_failures` is true, the flag `--strict-network` fails on and the install-time summary's "could not be checked" block reads. True for `metadata_unavailable` (every reason, `offline` and `install_time_budget` included), `monorepo_parent_unavailable`, `repository_activity_rate_limited`, `repository_activity_unreachable`, and an `advisories_unavailable` whose repository could not be reached; false for an `advisories_unavailable` whose repository answered with something lockrot could not read, and for every other code. The root `network_failures` is true exactly when some entry's is.

data.description: The facts behind the note, typed per `code`; `{}` for a code that has none. Every key a listed code's data declares is always written.

anyOf.description: A note whose code this schema does not list, from a later release or not from lockrot: its data is any object. Every code the schema lists is typed by its own branch above and cannot take this one.

noteCode.description: What a run note is about. lockrot's codes are lower-case words; `<vendor>:<name>` is reserved for a note that does not come from lockrot, as it is for a signal id. A kind, not an identifier: a run writes one code once per forge, per Composer repository or per monorepo parent it concerns. A code keeps its meaning (a new meaning gets a new code) and is retired, never removed or reused. An open set: a later minor release can add a code; read one you do not know as another thing the run could not see.

forgeId.description: The kind of repository host a note is about: `github`, `gitlab` (gitlab.com and every host in Composer's `gitlab-domains`) or `bitbucket`. An open set: a later release can add a host; read one you do not know as "other". The display name (`GitHub`) is the explanation's `activity.forge`, which is not this set.

metadataFailureReason.description: Why metadata did not come: `offline` (`--offline`, and Composer's cache had no copy), `install_time_budget` (the install-time budget ran out before the package was asked for), `no_versions` (the repository lists the package, and no version it serves is left), `fetch_failed` (any failure not given a more specific reason: a transport error, or what a repository threw, also under `--offline`; a later minor release may move cases out of it into new reasons). `message` carries the words. An open set: read a reason you do not know as another failure.

advisoriesNotCheckedReason.description: Why security advisories were not checked: `offline` (`--offline`; advisories are never served from a cache), `composer_too_old` (Composer below 2.4 has no advisory API), `install_time_budget` (the install-time budget ran out). An open set: read a reason you do not know as another reason.

repositoryActivityNotCheckedReason.description: Why no repository host was asked about activity at all: `install_time_budget` (the metadata pass used the whole install-time budget). An open set: read a reason you do not know as another reason.

forgeRepository.description: One repository on a repository host, with the keys S3 and S4 use: `host` as Composer names it (`github.com`, `gitlab.example.org`, possibly with a port or a path prefix) and `repo`, the path there (`owner/repo`, or `group/sub/project` on GitLab).

failedForgeRepository.description: One repository on a repository host that got no answer, with what the host said or the transport error, as `forgeRepository` plus `message`.

message.description: Foreign text — a repository's, a host's or Composer's own words — possibly empty, as a report may quote it: every URL in it without its userinfo, query and fragment, and every path on the machine down to its last segment (`.../name`); a message lockrot could not read whole is `(withheld: lockrot could not redact this message)`. Not contract.

noteOffline.description: `offline`: the run was `--offline`, so repository metadata came from Composer's cache. No parameters.

noteMetadataUnavailable.description: `metadata_unavailable`: metadata was asked for and did not come for `package_count` packages. `reasons` groups them by message, in the order the text lists them, and their `package_count`s sum to the note's. Each such finding is `unknown`, with `libyears_unmeasured` `metadata_unavailable`.

message.description: Foreign text — a repository's, a host's or Composer's own words — possibly empty, as a report may quote it: every URL in it without its userinfo, query and fragment, and every path on the machine down to its last segment (`.../name`); a message lockrot could not read whole is `(withheld: lockrot could not redact this message)`. Not contract.

noteMonorepoParentUnavailable.description: `monorepo_parent_unavailable`: the monorepo whose tags date the packages split out of it could not be loaded, so their dates are their own. `parent` is the package a finding's `dated_by` would have named.

message.description: Foreign text — a repository's, a host's or Composer's own words — possibly empty, as a report may quote it: every URL in it without its userinfo, query and fragment, and every path on the machine down to its last segment (`.../name`); a message lockrot could not read whole is `(withheld: lockrot could not redact this message)`. Not contract.

noteAdvisoryIgnoreUnreadable.description: `advisory_ignore_unreadable`: Composer rejected the project's advisory ignore configuration, so every advisory counts. `message` is the first line of what Composer said.

message.description: Composer's own words about the project's `audit` or `policy` configuration, the first line, possibly empty; they quote that configuration, never a repository. Not contract.

noteAdvisoriesDisabledByPolicy.description: `advisories_disabled_by_policy`: the project's Composer policy stops Composer from warning about security advisories. The note is information only. lockrot writes it only when the lookup ran. lockrot asked its repositories as usual, and the advisories they returned count. `policy_key` names the setting: `policy`, `policy.advisories`, `policy.advisories.audit` or the `COMPOSER_POLICY` environment variable. `value` is `false`, or `ignore` for the audit mode. The keys are an open set. Show a key you do not know as written.

noteAdvisoriesUnavailable.description: `advisories_unavailable`: one Composer repository did not return advisories, and the others were still asked. `composer_repository` is Composer's name for it, its URL cut as `message` cuts one; `message` the first line of the error, or its class when it has none.

message.description: Foreign text — a repository's, a host's or Composer's own words — possibly empty, as a report may quote it: every URL in it without its userinfo, query and fragment, and every path on the machine down to its last segment (`.../name`); a message lockrot could not read whole is `(withheld: lockrot could not redact this message)`. Not contract.

noteAdvisoriesNotChecked.description: `advisories_not_checked`: no advisory was looked for past this point, so a priority an advisory would raise stays one step lower. `composer_repositories_checked` counts the advisory-capable repositories lockrot asked before the check stopped, whatever each gave: advisories, none at all, or a failure, which has its own `advisories_unavailable` note. Always 0 for `offline` and `composer_too_old`; above 0 under `install_time_budget`, the check was partial: the advisories those repositories returned are in the findings, and the rest were never asked.

noteRepositoryActivityNotChecked.description: `repository_activity_not_checked`: no repository host was asked about activity; the findings it concerns carry S10 with the same `reason`.

noteRepositoryActivityAnonymousCap.description: `repository_activity_anonymous_cap`: without credentials for the host the run asked only about candidate packages, and at most a budget of them: `checked` were asked, `skipped_no_token` were not candidates (S10 `no_token` on their findings) and `skipped_budget` were candidates beyond the budget (S10 `anonymous_budget`). The text prints the two skipped counts as one sum. GitLab has no cap.

noteRepositoryActivityRateLimited.description: `repository_activity_rate_limited`: a host of this kind answered "too many requests". `repositories` lists every repository of this kind of host that got no answer, on each of its hosts, with its own message; the text's count is its length. Every package on this kind of host whose activity is missing carries S10 `rate_limit`, one whose repository answered 404 (listed under `repository_activity_not_found`) included.

noteRepositoryActivityUnreachable.description: `repository_activity_unreachable`: the host did not answer for `repositories`, each with its own message; the text prints their count and the first one's message. Their findings carry S10 `fetch_failed`.

noteRepositoryActivityNotFound.description: `repository_activity_not_found`: the host answered 404 for `repositories` (private, renamed or removed). An answer, not a network failure; where the host did not also rate-limit, this is the only record of them: their findings carry no S10 and their explanation's `activity` is null.

noteNotFromComposerRepository.description: `not_from_composer_repository`: `package_count` packages carry no Composer notification-url, and lockrot asked no repository about them. Equal to the report's `not_from_composer_repository`.
